reviews.text: Oh my dogs!

Flock of dogs is quirky and fun, best experienced as couch multiplayer. There is lots to do. The early access minigames just peaks my intrigue. I'm very excited for the real adventure to begin. It's a co-op crew game where your mothership is a whale and you can pilot individual spaceships in the form of flying dogs. A rogue-like spiritual successor to FTL, but operating in real-time and allowing you to play with your friends in a party game environment. The style and graphics are intensely unique, quite possibly we have entered the solo dev's recurring dreamworld. Quick to learn and easily accessible to casual gamers as well. I am organizing a game night to play this with some friends (my flock). I don't know where it will lead, but I do know I will customize my dog to match my RL mini-poodle and go full Leeroy into some really unique looking monsters, especially if I find that punching glove thing.

Disclaimer: I'm friends with the dev, and my current playtime hours come from playtesting the game. Flock of Dogs is a game made with soul, and has made me smile and laugh many times over. Designing an absurd race track with friends. Watching the dramatic activation sequence of the Build-A-Pup 3000. Stealing Tetris pieces from the opposing team's whale's belly. Flying around on a kite. Drawing stuff. Tossing squeaky balls for dogs. The game is inspired by Dr. Seuss, but it definitely has a style and quirkiness of its own. It's definitely worth giving a spin with friends, and keeping an eye on its progress while its in Early Access. Especially for the future Festival DLC, which is a co-op adventure where you fight enemies. Note that in its current state, you may encounter some technical issues, but these are expected during Early Access, and the dev works hard to fix issues.

Flock of Dogs is delightful. I've really enjoyed playing the mini games with friends locally and online. The Seuss inspired artwork is charming and the game is very approachable for people of all ages. If you have younger children in the house I can definitely see you spending many hours playing these games with them. A neat thing about the mini games is that the rules aren't strictly enforced. It feels a lot like an outdoor playground and you can make up your own rules as you play! Definitely check it out. I'm excited because this is just the beginning and the full Flight to the Festival DLC is still coming -- can't wait!

I cannot stress enough, this game is amazing. I was expecting this to be another under developed indie title being given out for free on keymailer but it entirely exceeded my expectations. It has an adorable and nostalgic aesthetic based off of Dr. Seuss' books and it adds a lot to the charm. There are a lot of unique ideas implemented here and I can't wait to see more content out of this. I have played a LOT of roguelikes and this has made my list of hidden gems. All this is not to say it doesn't have some flaws, the controls can be a little awkward sometimes, I found myself accidentally interacting with objects near what I intended. The online multiplayer can be odd, my friend that I was playing with had a complete map desync and he had to leave the lobby and come back. Having to leave the lobby isn't a big deal as the multiplayer is drop in. I would love to see more power ups for the player character and an improved system for the learnable dog traits. More weapons would be a plus. There's so much potential here that it's staggering, I am so excited to see where this goes from here.

I did receive a free key for this game to stream on my Twitch channel, but all thoughts and opinions on the game are entirely my own :) This game... is goofy. Really, you should know that just looking at it. You ride dogs. Your base is a whale. You shoot at weird little creatures in the sky, attempting to get to a festival. What's serious about it? My friend and I were laughing the entire time we played. The story is incredibly minimal - you're gathering these tiny little creatures in procedurally generated... dungeons? areas? in an attempt to bring them to a festival. Depending on your difficulty, you are also trying to free band members to go on the stage - however, we died swiftly on normal, so baby easy mode we meant, meaning no band - for which they rightfully ridicule you on when you reach the end. You start the game with a bit of a tutorial, but in my opinion... not enough of a tutorial. We were both very lost when we got to the actual game, BUT, despite our singular shared braincell, were able to figure it out and beat the game our second run. It was mostly straight forward and just trial and error. Despite the confusion, we didn't really get frustrated - if anything, our failures had us laughing more. I will say, this game is buggy. I think the devs are aware, as they have a place in game to populate all teh errors the game has sent itself, and send them along to the devs. Based on the minimal interactions I had with at least one member of the team pre-stream, they seemed very well meaning, and there have already been multiple updates to fix bugs. Despite what at the beginning felt like a GAME BREAKING bug of my friend and I seeming to generate entirely different dungeons (we saw different things on our screens), we still managed to fly our whale to victory and honestly have a great time! One absolute plus to this game is that owning the game allows for a friend to play with you. They simple need to download the friend pass version of the game from the story, and they can join you. Which is great, as I think this game would not be nearly as fun solo. Each key owned allows for one friend to join, so if 4 friends own the game, you can get a full squad of 8! I can only imagine the chaos of that many people - it seems like a great time. I think that the price point of this game is pretty fair. You can keep playing over and over thanks to the procedural generation, and with friends this game is so GOOFY and FUN. I'm very grateful for the chance to have played this game, and definitely plan to again :)

"Flock of Dogs" is a failed attempt to make a quirky 2D hand drawn action/party game ripping off themes from Dr Seuss. There's some minigames and top down action/arcade type gameplay and wacky flying gods that, yes, live on a whale. Ok whatever. This ostensibly failed because while the art concept is charming, the delivery is clunky, and the animations are pretty poor. The graphics in this game are passable, but could be better. And while it's vital for any game to have impressive visuals (gaming is a visual medium, after all), there's more to a game than just the graphics. To be worth a gamers time, the game must match top tier visuals with top tier gameplay, and that's not happening here. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. There's no initial download price, but the developer was charging $10 USD for this. Price barriers, especially on low quality products, can be a direct cause of failure. It seems like a nice gesture for the game to have no up-front cost anymore, but it also tells us that the game wasn't good enough to succeed as a paid product. Even after that, this still isn't really free as you're expected to pay up more money (up to $18 USD) to unlock content/DLC so you can keep playing. This is some predatory, misleading pricing on a non-free product. Despite having no up-front cost, this failed to appeal to the 120 million+ gamers on Steam. SteamDB showed the game peaked at just a dozen or so concurrent players, and now there's basically nobody playing it. Even though it's free. This is a dismal public reception, but it's easy to see why gamers rejected it. It's important to note that, despite this being such a low quality product, there's a number of positive reviews that all appeared immediately after the game launched, from suspiciously inactive Steam accounts that have reviewed almost no other games apart from this. Take the review score of this game with a grain of salt. Bearing in mind that free games don't add +1 to your game collector count, should you bother adding this to your library and downloading it? This isn't really a "free" game, it's got mobile app tier predatory pricing, which is the kind of thing PC gamers hate. That's just another reason not to bother downloading this "free" game.
